title: Deeper Still, Where Roots Remember Having Been Sky

features.name: the-inverted-tree
features.desc-on-touch: a tree grows downward from a ceiling of earth—roots hanging into air like branches, leaves dissolving into soil above. you understand it has no memory of being inverted; to it, this was always how sky descended.

features.name: the-silhouette-that-learned-to-speak
features.desc-on-touch: a shape cut from paper or cloth casts a shadow that doesn't match its outline. the shadow speaks in a voice that isn't its own, telling stories about a place that's always inverted. sometimes the shadow becomes more real than the object.

features.name: the-water-that-rises-downward
features.desc-on-touch: water pools on the underside of stone, held there as if gravity had reversed. insects skim its surface from below. you see reflections of a sky that exists deeper than this place—a sky below, a ground above.

features.name: the-fence-rows-that-remember-planting
features.desc-on-touch: rows of markers or posts stretching into the dark—a plantation grid, but the rows point downward, not across. each marker remembers being a seed, a sprout, a growth—all compressed into a vertical line. the rows have become a language of downward-growth.

features.name: the-hollow-that-grows-inward
features.desc-on-touch: a hollow in a massive root-system has become a dwelling, but the walls curve inward—space compresses as you go deeper. those who enter spend longer than they should, emerging confused about which direction is out.

inscription: growth remembers descending. everything that fell learned to call it flying.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the night you taught the roots which way was up
narr: katita stood beneath the inverted tree—she called it an 'inversion
study'—and leif asked which direction was falling. she smiled.
roots above them glowed faintly, photosynthesizing downlight from a
sun that no longer existed. 'they remember being sky,' she said.
'that's all memory is. the wrong direction, held perfectly.'
